transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have a civil subpoena on hand requesting customer analytics records, related communications, and a source-code appendix, with a written response due within 10 calendar days. Before I approve our response strategy and any commitments we make to the requesting party, I need each of you to report any issues that must be addressed. Let's go around the table — investigations, e-discovery, and business litigation liaison, please walk me through what you're seeing.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag a conflict issue before we go further. I completed a conflict-database check this morning and confirmed that our usual outside litigation firm, Harrison & Cole, currently represents the subpoenaing party in an unrelated matter. That creates a conflict preventing Harrison & Cole from advising us on this subpoena. I've already cleared Merritt Legal as the replacement firm, but I had not yet circulated this result before this meeting.

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag an issue from e-discovery. My document review of the responsive collection found exactly 47 attorney-client privileged emails and exactly 312 customer records containing Social Security numbers. These counts have not yet been added to the draft response spreadsheet because quality control of the export finished after the spreadsheet was sent to the case team. We need to address both the privilege review — to ensure those 47 emails are withheld or logged appropriately — and the SSN-containing records, which raise a data privacy concern before we produce any customer analytics records.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag an issue on the source-code appendix. During yesterday's meeting, the product vice president instructed me that the source-code appendix must not be produced until a protective order restricting access to outside counsel and experts is entered. The appendix contains the unreleased scoring logic that the product team considers its most sensitive trade secret. I have not yet incorporated that instruction into the response draft, so as it currently stands, the draft does not reflect this holdback condition.

commitments.detail: Engage Merritt Legal as outside counsel for this subpoena response in place of Harrison & Cole, which is conflicted due to its representation of the subpoenaing party in an unrelated matter.
Withhold or log all 47 attorney-client privileged emails identified in the document review; none will be produced without privilege protection.
Redact or otherwise protect all 312 customer records containing Social Security numbers before any customer analytics records are produced.
The source-code appendix will not be produced until a protective order restricting access to outside counsel and experts only is entered, to protect the unreleased scoring logic trade secret.
